title: Why a plain VERSION file remains a useful release signal
author: Kody Wildfeuer (@kody-w)
summary: A plain semantic-version file gives installers, the runtime, and reviewers one inspectable release signal without turning a version lookup into a hidden service dependency.
audience: Release owners and contributors who need a transparent, repeatable upgrade signal for a local-first runtime.
prerequisites: A local clone, Git, and permission to inspect the release branch and installer diff before promotion.
applicability: Applies when one local-first runtime needs one inspectable version signal shared by installers, health checks, and release reviewers.
support_boundary: Version comparison is informational; support and compatibility decisions still require reviewed release notes, tests, and environment-specific validation.
limitations: A version comparison does not replace release notes, compatibility testing, security review, or inspection of configuration and dependency changes.
